## Context

Story `f161-c70a-1a69-4ed1` landed the measurement-provenance mechanism: the deterministic
presence/shape check (`det_measurement_provenance.py`, advisory via `p6_ac_quality`), the
`.rebar/` overlay routing entry (advisory, `exec: AGENT`, `[operator-attested]` trigger), the
`execution_mode: agentic` rubric stating decision rules (a)-(d), and ADR-0061.

What it did NOT deliver is any proof that the AGENT criterion actually FIRES or STAYS SILENT as
the rubric specifies. The rubric states the rules; nothing exercises them. Every sibling project
criterion ships a `.rebar/evals/<prompt-id>.eval.yaml`; this one has none.

This was descoped from f161 deliberately: the criterion ships **advisory**, so the mechanism is
correct and useful without calibration, and the ADR-0054 promotion decision it feeds is not being
made yet. Filed as an **idea** because promotion is a judgement call nobody has committed to.

## Approach

Follow the `project.engine-layer-enforcement` pattern exactly (`.rebar/evals/REDACTED_TOKEN.eval.yaml`
+ its offline shape test + a live semantic run recorded as attested evidence).

**1. `.rebar/evals/REDACTED_TOKEN.eval.yaml`** — a BALANCED corpus,
`epochs: 3`, `gate: at_least(2)`, a deterministic `emits_valid_findings` scorer. Each entry needs a
`note` naming the causal mechanism and observable effect, not just a label. Minimum fixtures:

| Rule | Fixture | expect |
|---|---|---|
| (a) environment contradiction | declares `579718921998`, repo Terraform backend names `896586841071` | finding |
| (a) contrast | declared account MATCHES the IaC | pass |
| (b) no-anchor fallback | non-AWS cluster/tenant id with no in-repo counterpart | pass |
| (c) privilege posture | scoped-permission criterion declaring `privilege_posture=broader` | finding |
| (c) contrast | same criterion declaring `production-equivalent` | pass |
| (d) instrument vs claim | AUTHORIZATION claim + `instrument=simulation` **at** `privilege_posture=production-equivalent` | finding |
| (d) contrast | same claim with `instrument=live-call` | pass |

The (d) must-fire case is the load-bearing one: it is the ONLY fixture that proves `instrument` is
judged INDEPENDENTLY of `privilege_posture`. Both fields read 'fine' in it, and it must still fire —
that is escape 2b (`simulate-principal-policy` returning a confident WRONG authorization answer that
only a live call refuted). If this fixture passes when it should fire, the fourth field epic 3147
mandated is decorative.

**Fixture quality is the actual work.** A must-fire plan so obviously broken that any criterion
would flag it proves nothing. Each must-fire case should differ from its contrast case in ONE
declared field, so a fire/pass split isolates the rule under test.

**2. `tests/unit/REDACTED_TOKEN.py`** — offline shape checks, no LLM, CI-safe:
fixture parses, ids unique, `criterion` matches, both polarities present, every rule covered.

**3. Live semantic run** — `rebar criteria eval project.measurement-provenance --runs 3`, recorded on
this ticket as `[operator-attested]` evidence. Dogfood this epic's own contract: the attestation must
itself carry a `provenance:` line (environment / principal / privilege_posture / instrument), which
doubles as the cheapest possible test that the new four-field contract is writable in practice.

# RECOMMENDATION AWAITING OPERATOR APPROVAL — do not decompose or implement yet

Filed 2026-08-05 at the operator's request after a single session surfaced nine instances of one
defect family. The analysis and recommendation are below; the operator decides whether to adopt,
which stage to put it in, and whether to fund it.

## The family

Nine defects found in one session, all the same shape: **a check that cannot fail for the reason
it exists**. Not absent checks — present, passing, and load-bearing in someone's reasoning.

| ticket | instance |
|---|---|
| 34c2 | AST guard pinned to ONE file; a module split moved the policed construct away, and it passed unconditionally |
| 8a5e | four MORE of the same, found only by sweeping after 34c2. One was doubly vacuous: its literal line-prefixes could not match the absolute import spelling the code actually uses |
| 2c58 | inert-config gate matches bare attribute names GLOBALLY, so a field whose name is reused anywhere escapes it |
| 7e90 | CI gate hard-failed on definition-vs-tree skew; the governing rule existed only as a code COMMENT, and was violated within hours of being written |
| 1909 | ELEVEN more unguarded steps, two of them breaking builds live |
| c5b3 | the fake `scc` test double emitted per-file data unconditionally while real scc requires `--by-file` — so the one test positioned to catch a fabricated-zero bug was structurally blind to it |
| dce2, a573 | config fields with zero read sites; the gate that should have caught a573 could not, per 2c58 |
| 5e53 | module-size hard cap with NO leading indicator: 40 files over 700 LOC, three within two lines of a hard CI failure, every instance discovered by an already-blocked contributor |
| 858c | close gate cannot express an N/A criterion, forcing a tick that falsely asserts completion |

## Prior art — this recurred

It has been addressed before, and the tickets are CLOSED:
`6924-0034` (epic, "Post-migration test & CI quality hardening"), `4168-c28e`
("Mutation testing: identify and prune change-detector tests"), `003d-e6b0`
("Replace hasattr/constant existence tests with behavioral provocation"),
`0f8f-ec8a` ("tests overlay: full behavioral-testing standard"),
`5ef2-6e74` ("Rewrite tautological conflict-resolver echo-suppression test"),
`d006-759b` (module-size report "toothless").

That prior work was REMEDIAL — find the bad checks, fix them. It did not leave a mechanism that
prevents new ones, which is why the family is back. A recommendation that is only another sweep
will produce the same outcome in three months.

## Diagnosis: two sub-kinds needing different mechanisms

**A. Mechanically detectable** — scope rot (34c2, 8a5e), global-name matching (2c58), unguarded
steps (7e90, 1909), inert config (dce2, a573), missing leading indicator (5e53). In every case a
program can decide the question, because the check declares a target population and the
population is empty, wrong, or unbounded.

**B. Judgment-dependent** — test-double fidelity (c5b3), N/A expressiveness (858c). No sweep
finds these; they need a reader who understands what the check is FOR. c5b3's stub was
syntactically fine and passing.

## Recommendation

**Do BOTH, at two different stages. Neither alone is sufficient.**

**1. A CI structural meta-gate for sub-kind A — the higher-leverage half.**

Adopt as a repo-wide convention: *every scanning/structural check must declare its target
population and assert that population is NON-EMPTY and covers what it claims.* Then enforce that
in CI the way `1909` already proved works — parse, enumerate, fail on any check lacking the
assertion.

This is not speculative. Three enforcement gates of exactly this shape already exist and work:
1909's workflow-step sweep (with a vacuity assertion on the detector itself), the module-size
contract, and the 6754 config-read gate. The recommendation is to generalize a proven local
pattern, not invent one.

Put it in **CI, not plan review** — plan review runs before code exists and cannot verify a
population; and **not completion verification**, which reads narrative evidence rather than code.

**2. A code-review criterion for sub-kind B.**

Something close to: *"Does this change add or modify a check — a test, guard, gate, or test
double? If so, does it demonstrate the check can FAIL for the reason it exists, and does any
double model the real thing's CONSTRAINTS rather than only its happy path?"*

Code review is the right stage because it sees the diff and can reason about intent. It should be
ADVISORY first, not blocking, until its false-positive rate is known.

**3. The cross-cutting change, and the cheapest one: make mutation proof the expectation for
check-modifying changes.**

Every genuinely trustworthy fix this session did this VOLUNTARILY — 8a5e, 7e90, 1909 and c5b3 all
mutation-checked in both directions, and in 8a5e's case the decisive evidence was that the
SUPERSEDED predicate stayed GREEN under the same mutation. That contrast is what distinguishes
"the guard is clean" from "the guard is vacuous", and nothing in the current lifecycle asks for
it. Making it expected rather than exceptional is the single highest-value item here and costs
almost nothing to state.

## What I would NOT do

- **Not another remediation sweep alone.** That is what the closed prior-art tickets did.
- **Not a blocking gate on day one.** A false-positive-prone blocking check on "is this check
  vacuous" would itself become something people route around.
- **Not plan review.** Wrong stage; it cannot see the code.
- **Not one ticket per instance.** That is the pattern that produced 5e53's forty-file backlog and
  three separate one-file emergencies in one session.

## Open questions for the operator

- Adopt one, two, or all three parts?
- Should the CI meta-gate be blocking from the start, or warn-only until its noise is measured?
- Is the anti-vacuity convention worth retrofitting to existing checks (a bounded sweep), or
  applied only to new and modified ones going forward?

## Not acceptance criteria yet

Deliberately none. This ticket is a recommendation for approval; ACs should be written after the
operator decides scope, since the shape differs substantially between the three parts.

## Question
"How can we reduce the wall-clock runtime of our Gerrit Verified Gate on GitHub Actions
without reducing our coverage?" Operator later reported real gate times of 41-47 min.

## What the measurements showed
- Critical path was ONE job: `pytest (macos-latest, py3.13)` at 18.6m (run #1823 /
  id 30569775555). Every other job <=8m; without macOS the run finishes in ~8m.
- Within it: setup 0.7m, twelve drift gates ~0.1m, default pytest tier 15.4m, integration 2.0m.
- 7856 tests: ubuntu 5:04 at -n 4 vs macOS 15:21 at -n 3 — a 3x wall gap against a 1.33x vCPU gap.
- Dispatch lag from Gerrit is NOT a factor: change 1052 ps1 uploaded 18:24:36, run created
  18:24:38 (2s), Verified+1 at 18:53:35 = 29.0m, matching GitHub's own run_duration_ms.
- THE BINDING CONSTRAINT: navapbc is on GitHub Free = 20 concurrent jobs / 5 macOS,
  enforced PER ORGANIZATION, shared with every other navapbc repo. A single Verified run
  needs 21 job slots — one run alone cannot fully parallelize. Six changes dispatched within
  10 seconds queued 6.7-8.4m each for a macOS slot. That queue is the 41-47m.
- Peak concurrent macOS jobs observed across 25 sampled jobs: 4, never more.

| 1056 | f3d4 | coverage collected on ubuntu cells only (measured +5.1% overhead, so ~0.8m) |

## Load-bearing facts discovered (cite these, don't re-derive)
- **The Verified gate CANNOT exercise a change to `.github/workflows/**`.** `uses:
  ./.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` resolves from the DEFAULT BRANCH under
  workflow_dispatch; the patchset is only checked out INSIDE jobs. A flat pre-merge number is
  not evidence a workflow change did nothing — verified by dumping the macOS command line on
  1056's own run and finding `--cov` still present.
- **The working pre-merge lane for workflow changes is a SCRATCH BRANCH push to the mirror**
  (`optionality.yml` triggers on push, branches-ignore feature/**). A PULL REQUEST does not
  work: `.github/workflows/lockdown.yml` runs repo-lockdown on pull_request_target with
  close-pr: true. Used successfully on 1066 (run 30591336796).
- **Bare `git worktree repair` is DESTRUCTIVE, not a silent no-op.** Run inside a copy it
  rewrites the SOURCE's `.tickets-tracker/.git` to point into the copy.
- **`--git-common-dir` is green on a half-fixed store copy.** It derives from
  `.tickets-tracker/.git` alone and cannot witness a stale `gitdir`. Use
  `git worktree list --porcelain` containment.
- **`conftest` is not a stable module name.** Several conftests share it; under xdist
  `sys.modules["conftest"]` binds to whichever was imported last. `from conftest import X`
  works when a tier runs alone and fails in a full-suite run. Hence
  `tests/interfaces/_store_template.py`.
- **`init._gen_local_files()` is idempotency-guarded** (`if not os.path.isfile`), so calling
  it to re-mint `.env-id`/`.signing-key` on a copy is a silent no-op.
- **The gate snapshot store is keyed by COMMIT SHA ALONE** (`_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`), so
  a shared template SHA collapses ~150 gate-touching tests onto one entry. `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`
  is set per test.
- **`_optional.EXTRAS` != the old per-extra matrix list.** EXTRAS = {agents, eval, grounding,
  metrics, tracing}; `mcp` is NOT in it (no probe; validated by its boot check).
- **The literal `|| { rc=1; ...; continue; }` accumulator trips shellcheck SC2015** through
  actionlint and fails `make lint`. Use `if ! { ...; }; then ...; fi`.

## Discovered while landing bug 9f63

`89d5-61da-b621-47f8` owns the py3.11 CI cell instability, but it is CLOSED, so this preventable defect would otherwise live only as a comment on a closed ticket. Filing it open, because it is a guard we do not have and it cost a landing cycle.

## What happened

A new test in `tests/unit/test_review_bot_in_flight.py` used the idiomatic-looking

```python
with TestClient(app) as client:
    ...
```

to assert ONE field of the `/health` JSON body. Entering `TestClient` as a context manager runs the app **lifespan**, which:

* starts the queue worker,
* starts the **real** `reconcile_loop` (`app.py`) — every other lifespan-entering test in that module stubs it with `_idle_reconcile_loop` (`tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1462, :1490, :1631`),
* starts the snapshot janitor, whose `startup_sweep` is a genuine filesystem walk (`src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:282` -> `src/rebar/_snapshot/cache.py:133 entry_size`),
* and on exit awaits `queue.join()` under `shutdown_drain_seconds()` — a **1200-second** window.

Under coverage tracing on the py3.11 cell that combination wedged an xdist worker. The suite reached 99% and produced no further output until the 60-minute job timeout, three runs in a row.

## Why it was expensive to find

It presents exactly like the runner-side flake it is not. Three of four matrix cells passed; the review-bot test files passed in isolation; the full suite passed on 3.11 *without* `--cov`. Only the complete CI command reproduces it. Attribution needed a controlled A/B:

| tree | py3.11 + coverage + xdist, CI's exact command |
| --- | --- |
| clean `origin/main` @ 1afdbbd0be | 11184 passed, 26 skipped, **16m11s** |
| the branch | **hung at 99%** |

and then `faulthandler` (`timeout -s ABRT`) to see a worker holding a live anyio blocking portal alongside the janitor thread mid-sweep.

## Why a guard is worth it

Nothing in the repo makes any of this visible at the call site. `with TestClient(app)` reads like a normal client construction; the 20-minute drain, the live reconciler and the disk walk are all invisible consequences. The existing convention — stub `reconcile_loop` — is real but undocumented and unenforced, so it is followed by imitation and lost by anyone who writes a fresh test.

## Fix sketch

Cheapest useful version, in rough order of value:

1. A shared fixture (e.g. `review_bot_client`) that enters the lifespan with `reconcile_loop` stubbed, the janitor disabled and `shutdown_drain_seconds` overridden to something test-scaled, so the safe path is also the easy path.
2. A test-lint or `conftest` assertion that fails fast when the review-bot app lifespan is entered without the reconciler stub, naming the fixture to use.
3. Prefer awaiting the handler directly when a test only asserts a response payload — the route returns the dict as-is, so the contract is identical and nothing background starts. (That is what bug 9f63's change ended up doing.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test that enters the review-bot app lifespan without stubbing `reconcile_loop` fails fast with a message naming the correct fixture, rather than hanging
- [ ] The shared fixture bounds `shutdown_drain_seconds` to a test-scaled value, proven by a test asserting the teardown completes in seconds
- [ ] The snapshot janitor does not perform a real filesystem sweep under that fixture
- [ ] The convention is stated where a test author will see it, not only inherited by imitation

## Root cause of the churn (measured on two consecutive revisions)

Between consecutive writes the file grows only **+2,470 bytes**, and only **1,229 added / 1,166 deleted lines out of 526,487 (0.45%)**. But of those ~2,395 changed lines, **2,290 are `baseline_advanced_at` timestamp updates** - 96%% of the churn. The remaining ~69 lines are real change (`type`, `text`, `last_get_pass`).

In one file version there are 1,507 `baseline_advanced_at` occurrences with 230 distinct values - but **1,145 of them carry the SAME value**, bumped together on each pass. It is one logical fact (this pass advanced the baseline at time T) physically duplicated across ~1,145 binding entries.

The field is only 0.4%% of the file's bytes, but the edits are SCATTERED across all 18 MB, so every reconcile produces a delta with ~1,145 separate change regions. That is what defeats delta compression and yields 252 KB packed per version.

## Why the obvious remedies do not work

- **Aggressive repack will not help materially.** The blobs are ALREADY deltified: 8,157 of 8,165 bridge-state blobs have delta depth > 0 (avg depth 13.9) and still occupy 940.5 MB. Only 8 blobs (1.9 MB) are non-deltified. There is essentially no delta headroom left.
- **`git gc`** reclaims only the 3 stray `tmp_pack_*` files (3.67 MiB) and consolidates 14 packs. Free, but small.
- **History rewrite** would reclaim the most but is unsafe: `tickets` is the shared source of truth and rewriting it breaks every clone.

## Fix direction (stops the bleeding; safe, no history rewrite)

Stop rewriting a per-binding field that is really one global fact:
1. Hoist `baseline_advanced_at` to a single top-level value (per pass), leaving per-binding entries untouched when nothing about that binding changed; or
2. only update a binding's `baseline_advanced_at` when that binding actually changed.

Either collapses per-reconcile churn from ~2,395 changed lines to ~69, which should cut new-version delta cost by roughly 97%%.

Worth considering alongside: whether `prev_snapshot.json` (26 MB, 5,151 versions, 202 MB packed) needs to be versioned at all, or is a derived cache that could live outside git.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A reconcile pass that changes N bindings produces a bindings.json diff proportional to N, not to the total binding count.
- [ ] Measured: consecutive-revision changed-line count drops from ~2,395 to the order of the number of genuinely-changed bindings.
- [ ] A decision is recorded on whether `prev_snapshot.json` must be committed at all.
- [ ] No change to reconciler correctness: binding resolution and baseline semantics are unchanged (covered by existing reconciler tests).

`_engine_support/validate.py` carried `elif arg == "--fix": pass  # accepted, no-op (the bash --fix path is unimplemented)`. Maintainer decision was REMOVE, not implement: `doctor` is the fixing path. Removed under 7be3; `--fix` now falls through validate's existing unknown-option handler (`Unknown option: --fix`, exit 1), and both runtime hints now point at `rebar doctor`.

`rebar doctor` is dispatched only from `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:323`. Outside the CLI dispatch plus its own help text and generated reference, the only mentions in the repo are prose: `CHANGELOG.md` (the entry announcing it) and `docs/ticket-model.md` (two lines describing the blocking-link audit). No script, CI workflow, Makefile target, agent skill, or AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING guidance ever tells anyone to run it. So the command the project designates as "the path for fixing" has no adoption surface at all — that gap is arguably more load-bearing for this consolidation than the naming overlap.

Worse, the non-interactive environment is not merely missing the key; it carries a DIFFERENT, INVALID one that shadows it. That value does not come from the usual non-interactive startup files: ~/.zshenv, ~/.zprofile and ~/.profile each contain ZERO references to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. So it is being injected into the process environment upstream — inherited from the launching process, a LaunchAgent, or an editor/tool environment — and needs to be traced there.

Why this matters beyond this ticket: every measurement taken against the direct-Anthropic arm in a non-interactive context has been measuring an invalid credential, not the provider. That contaminates the provider-comparison evidence on 1e88 and 2391 in a way neither ticket currently accounts for — both assume the arm was exercised.

Remediation shape (NOT yet implemented, needs an operator call): an exported credential that gates depend on should live where non-interactive shells actually read it (~/.zshenv rather than ~/.zshrc), or be resolved by rebar from a credential store rather than inherited from the ambient environment. Until then, AC3's preflight cannot pass in the context that actually runs it — and note a preflight that probes the key would have caught this instantly, which is an argument for AC4.

No key value was read, printed, or logged in producing this evidence — identity was compared by hash and validity by HTTP status only.
